examples.ko: 여름에는 아스팔트가 뜨거워서 맨발로 못 걸어요.
examples.en: In summer the asphalt is too hot to walk on barefoot.
They laid new asphalt on the road.
When it rains, you can smell the asphalt.

examples.ko: 아스팔트 위에 물이 고여서 길이 미끄러워요.
examples.en: Water has collected on the asphalt, so the road is slippery.

examples.ko: 한여름 아스팔트에서는 강아지 산책을 피하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: In midsummer it's best to avoid walking your dog on asphalt.
A road paved with asphalt is easy to walk on.

explain: 도로를 만드는 재료라서 '아스팔트 도로', '아스팔트 길'처럼 써요. 흙길과 달리 포장된 길을 떠올리면 돼요. 검고 열을 잘 받아서 여름 더위나 강아지 산책 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 집 앞에 새 아스팔트 도로가 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A new asphalt road was built in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장된 길을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a paved road.

phrases.example: 공사 때문에 길에 아스팔트를 깔고 있어요.
phrases.en: They are laying asphalt on the road for construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로를 새로 포장하는 작업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the work of paving a road.

phrases.example: 뜨거운 아스팔트 위를 걸으면 강아지 발이 아파요.
phrases.en: Walking on hot asphalt hurts a dog's paws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름 더위를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about summer heat.

explain_en: Because it is a road-building material, it appears in phrases like '아스팔트 도로' and '아스팔트 길'. Think of a paved road, as opposed to a dirt path. It is black and absorbs heat, so it often comes up in talk about summer heat and walking dogs.

examples.en: I found old newspapers in the school resource room.
Reports and photos are organized in the resource room.

examples.ko: 필요한 파일은 회사 자료실에 올려 두세요.
examples.en: Please upload the files you need to the company's resource section.

examples.ko: 도서관 자료실이 몇 시에 문을 열어요?
examples.en: What time does the library's reference room open?
I went to the reference room and copied an old article.

examples.ko: 자료실 컴퓨터는 학생들이 자유롭게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Students can freely use the computers in the resource room.

explain: '자료실'은 건물 안의 방뿐 아니라 웹사이트 메뉴 이름으로도 많이 써서, 파일을 올리고 받는 곳을 가리켜요. 책을 빌리는 곳은 '대출실', 조용히 공부하는 곳은 '열람실'이에요.

phrases.en: I uploaded the homework file to the resource page.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웹사이트의 자료실 메뉴에 파일을 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for putting a file in a website's resource section.
phrases.en_equiv: to upload to the resource room

phrases.en: You can download the form from the resource room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내려받다'와 함께 써서 파일을 받는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '내려받다', it names where to download files.
phrases.en_equiv: to get from the resource room

phrases.en: The resource room is open only on weekdays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 안의 방을 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for using the room inside a building.

explain_en: '자료실' is not only a room in a building; it is also a very common website menu name for the place where files are uploaded and downloaded. The place to borrow books is '대출실', and the quiet study area is '열람실'.

examples.ko: 삼촌 차는 산길도 잘 달리는 지프예요.
examples.en: My uncle's car is a jeep that runs well even on mountain roads.
The soldiers loaded their baggage onto the back of the jeep.

examples.ko: 지프는 차체가 높아서 눈길에도 잘 가요.
examples.en: A jeep sits high, so it goes well even on snowy roads.
It took an hour by jeep to get to the campsite.

examples.ko: 저기 서 있는 초록색 지프가 우리 차예요.
examples.en: The green jeep standing over there is our car.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 지프를 타고 사막을 달렸어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the hero drove across the desert in a jeep.

explain: 원래는 한 회사의 차 이름이지만, 한국어에서는 험한 길을 달리는 큰 차를 두루 '지프'라고 불러요. 요즘은 'SUV'라는 말도 많이 써요. 군인들이 타는 차 이야기에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Our family drives a big SUV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘은 '지프'보다 'SUV'라는 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nowadays 'SUV' is used more often than 지프.

phrases.en: A jeep is handy in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지프'와 같은 뜻이고, 뒤에 '차'를 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 지프, with 차 (car) added.

phrases.example: 여행 가서 지프를 타고 사막을 달렸어요.
phrases.en: On my trip, I rode a jeep across the desert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 험한 길을 달리는 차를 탈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for riding in a vehicle that handles rough roads.

explain_en: It started as a company's car name, but in Korean '지프' is used for big vehicles that run on rough roads in general. Today 'SUV' is also widely used. It also comes up often in talk about cars the military uses.

examples.ko: 다음 달 징검다리 연휴에는 하루만 쉬면 닷새를 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: During next month's bridge holiday, if I take just one day off, I get five days of rest.

examples.ko: 징검다리 연휴에 여행 가려고 비행기 표를 미리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought plane tickets in advance to travel over the bridge holiday.

examples.ko: 시냇물에 놓인 징검다리를 건너서 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: I crossed the stepping stones in the stream to get to school.
The children carefully hop across the stepping stones.

examples.ko: 이번 경험이 다음 도전의 징검다리가 될 거예요.
examples.en: This experience will be a stepping stone for your next challenge.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 징검다리가 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the stepping stones were under water.

explain: 개울에 돌을 띄엄띄엄 놓아 건너게 한 길을 말하고, 그래서 '다음 단계로 가게 해 주는 것'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 달력에서는 휴일 사이에 평일 하루가 끼인 연휴를 '징검다리 연휴'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이번 징검다리 연휴에는 하루 휴가를 내고 고향에 가요.
phrases.en: For this bridge holiday, I'm taking one day of leave and going to my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 날 사이에 평일이 하루나 이틀 끼어서 군데군데 쉬는 연휴를 말해요. 돌을 띄엄띄엄 밟고 건너는 모습에서 나왔어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A holiday period where one or two workdays sit between days off, so the rest comes in separated chunks. The image is of stepping across stones set at intervals.

explain_en: It names a path of stones laid at intervals so you can cross a stream, and so it is often used figuratively for something that takes you to the next step. On the calendar, a holiday stretch with a single workday between days off is called a '징검다리 연휴'.

examples.en: It was my first time sharing a taxi, so I was a bit nervous.
I went home late at night by sharing a ride.

examples.ko: 합승을 하면 요금을 나눠 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you share a ride, you can split the fare.
An app that allows ride sharing has come out.
How is the shared-ride fare calculated?
If you agree to share the ride, please press the button.

explain: 택시나 차를 모르는 사람과 같이 탈 때 많이 써요. '합승 요금', '합승 서비스'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙기도 해요. 동사로 말할 때는 '합승하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Sharing a taxi is hard at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택시를 다른 사람과 같이 타는 상황에서 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for sharing a taxi with other people.

phrases.en: We split the shared ride fare in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같이 탄 사람들이 나눠 내는 돈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the fare that riders split between them.

phrases.example: 요즘은 앱으로 합승 서비스를 이용할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Nowadays you can use a ride-sharing service through an app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 같은 차를 타도록 해 주는 서비스를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a service that lets several people ride in the same car.

explain_en: It is often used when you share a taxi or car with people you don't know. Other words can follow it, as in '합승 요금' or '합승 서비스'. As a verb, use '합승하다'.

examples.en: There is a camera at the back of the car.
Reverse parking is still hard for me.
The defenders pass the ball slowly at the back.
The ball rolled back and a defender caught it.

examples.ko: 후방이 안전해야 앞에서 마음 놓고 일할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only when the back is safe can people work freely at the front.
The rear sensor beeped, so I stopped the car.

explain: 사물이나 대열의 뒤쪽을 말하는 격식 있는 말이에요. 군대에서는 전선 뒤쪽을 '후방', 앞쪽을 '전방'이라고 해요. 운전할 때는 '후방 카메라', '후방 주차', '후방 감지기'로 자주 만나요. 일상에서 그냥 뒤를 말할 때는 '뒤', '뒤쪽'이 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I installed a rear sensor on my car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전할 때 뒤쪽 물건을 알려 주는 장치 이름으로 자주 만나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly seen as the name of a device that detects objects behind a car.

phrases.en: The soldiers waited in the rear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대 이야기에서는 전선 뒤쪽이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In military talk it means behind the front line.

phrases.en: I sat at the back of the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 그냥 뒤를 말할 때는 '후방'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is more natural than 후방 for simply saying the back.

explain_en: A formal word for the back of an object or formation. In the military, the area behind the front line is '후방' and the front is '전방'. In driving you meet it in '후방 카메라', '후방 주차', and '후방 감지기'. In everyday speech '뒤' or '뒤쪽' sounds much more natural.

t90.ax: Reverse parking is still hard for me.

examples.ko: 그 동굴은 아주 깊숙해서 불빛이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: That cave is so deep that light doesn't reach it.

examples.ko: 서랍이 깊숙해서 물건이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The drawer is deep, so I can't see things well.

examples.ko: 깊숙한 골목 안에 작은 카페가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe deep inside the alley.

examples.ko: 반지는 가방 깊숙한 곳에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put the ring deep inside my bag.
The deeper into the forest you go, the quieter it gets.

examples.ko: 산속 깊숙한 곳에 있던 그 절은 찾기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That temple tucked deep in the mountains was hard to find.

explain: '깊다'는 위에서 아래로 깊이를 말하고, '깊숙하다'는 바깥에서 안쪽으로 멀리 들어간 곳을 말해요. 그래서 서랍, 가방, 산속, 골목처럼 안으로 들어가는 곳에 어울려요. 보통 '깊숙한 곳', '깊숙이'로 써요.

phrases.en: The key is deep inside the bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안쪽으로 멀리 들어간 장소를 말할 때 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to a far-inside place.

phrases.en: I put my hand in deeply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작이 안쪽 멀리까지 닿는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an action that reaches far inside.

phrases.en: This drawer is not deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 안쪽이 그리 멀지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying the inside is not very far.

explain_en: 깊다 describes depth from top to bottom, while 깊숙하다 describes a spot that is far inside from the outside. That is why it suits drawers, bags, mountains and alleys. It usually appears as 깊숙한 곳 or 깊숙이.

t90.ax: I put the ring deep inside my bag.

en: to be safe; to be strong

examples.en: This bag is fine even in the rain.
I'm fine even if I stay up all night.
They say it's a sturdy building, so it won't budge even in an earthquake.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸린 친구들과 있어도 저는 끄떡없었어요.
examples.en: Even around friends with colds, I stayed perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 아무리 힘든 일이 닥쳐도 그는 끄떡없어 보여요.
examples.en: No matter how hard things get, he looks unshaken.
Will this phone be okay even if I drop it?

explain: 어떤 충격이나 힘든 일이 있어도 흔들리거나 상하지 않고 멀쩡한 상태를 말해요. 사람과 물건 모두에 쓰고, 보통 '~에도 끄떡없다', '~도 끄떡없다'로 말해요. 비슷한 '멀쩡하다'는 다치거나 고장 나지 않은 상태 자체를 말해요.

phrases.en: This phone is fine even if you drop it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충격에도 멀쩡하다고 말하는 기본 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form for saying something stays fine despite a shock.

phrases.en: They played outside, unaffected by the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 써서 어려움에도 흔들리지 않고 행동했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, meaning someone acted without being shaken by hardship.

phrases.example: 운동을 해서 감기에도 끄떡없는 몸이 됐어요.
phrases.en: I exercised, so my body became strong enough to resist even colds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '끄떡없는'으로 써서 튼튼함을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, use '끄떡없는' to show sturdiness.

explain_en: It describes staying unshaken and undamaged even when facing a shock or hardship. It is used for both people and things, usually as '~에도 끄떡없다' or '~도 끄떡없다'. The similar '멀쩡하다' focuses on simply being uninjured or not broken.

t90.ax: This bag is fine even in the rain.

examples.ko: 길이 부드러운 반원을 그리며 휘어 있어요.
examples.en: The road curves in a gentle semicircle.
The students sat in a semicircle in front of the teacher.
Try drawing a semicircle with a compass.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 반원 모양의 터널이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a semicircle-shaped tunnel under the bridge.
I cut the cake into a half-circle shape.
The diameter of a semicircle is the same as that of the circle.

explain: 원을 반으로 나눈 모양이에요. 의자 배치나 도형 문제에 자주 나와요. 모양을 말할 때는 '반달 모양'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I drew a semicircle in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도형이나 모양을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when drawing the shape.

phrases.en: The semicircle-shaped window is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the shape of an object.

phrases.en: The rice cake is shaped like a half-moon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반원과 비슷한 모양을 좀 더 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to describe a similar shape.

explain_en: It is the shape you get when you cut a circle in half. It often comes up in seating arrangements and geometry problems. For the shape, people also say '반달 모양' (half-moon shape).

examples.en: It's a sheer curtain, so some light comes in.

examples.ko: 이 비닐봉지는 반투명해서 안이 흐릿하게 보여요.
examples.en: This plastic bag is translucent, so the inside looks blurry.
The bathroom glass is frosted.
I put the snacks in a translucent plastic container.
I put a translucent film on the new window.
The ice turned translucent as it melted.

explain: '투명'은 뒤까지 다 보이고, '반투명'은 빛은 통하지만 모양이 흐릿하게 보여요. 반대말은 '불투명'이에요. '반투명 유리'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙이거나 '반투명하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The bathroom door is translucent glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 말 앞에 '반투명'을 붙여서 물건을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 반투명 before another noun to describe an object.

phrases.en: I drew a picture on translucent paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반투명하다'를 '-한'으로 바꾸면 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change 반투명하다 to -한 to describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이 컵은 불투명해서 안이 안 보여요.
phrases.en: This cup is opaque, so you can't see inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반투명의 반대말이고, 빛이 통하지 않아 안이 안 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 반투명; light doesn't pass, so you can't see through.

explain_en: '투명' lets you see through completely, while '반투명' lets light through but the shapes look blurry. The opposite is '불투명'. It is used before another noun, as in '반투명 유리', or as '반투명하다'.

examples.en: This watch is a little inaccurate with the time.
You shouldn't trust inaccurate information.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 내용이 부정확해서 다시 고쳤어요.
examples.en: The article's content was inaccurate, so it was corrected.
Isn't my pronunciation imprecise?

examples.ko: 부정확하게 말하면 오해가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak imprecisely, misunderstandings can arise.
The map must have been inaccurate, because I got lost.

explain: 반대말은 '정확하다'예요. '정확하지 않다'라고 풀어서 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. '틀리다'는 아예 맞지 않다는 뜻이라서, 대체로 맞지만 어딘가 모자랄 때는 '부정확하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 부정확한 설명 때문에 길을 잘못 들었어요.
phrases.en: I took the wrong road because of an inaccurate explanation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부정확한' 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a noun after '부정확한'.

phrases.en: This map is not accurate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부정확하다'와 뜻이 같고 말이 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '부정확하다' but easier wording.

phrases.example: 기억이 부정확해서 확실히 말할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: My memory is not accurate, so I can't say for sure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 '-아서/어서'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아서/어서' to give a reason.

explain_en: The opposite is '정확하다', and '정확하지 않다' says the same thing in two words. '틀리다' means completely wrong, so for something that is mostly right but not exact, use '부정확하다'.

examples.ko: 하늘이 잿빛으로 흐려서 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sky is clouded in ash-gray, so it looks like rain soon.
Gray clouds hang low.
The winter sea is gray, so it looks lonely.
Grandfather's hair has turned ash-gray before I knew it.
Wearing a gray coat makes me look calm.
That dog's fur is close to ash-gray.

explain: 검은색이 아니라 재처럼 탁한 회색이에요. 하늘, 구름, 바다, 도시처럼 흐리고 쓸쓸한 분위기에 자주 쓰고, 일반적인 색 이름은 '회색'이에요. 발음은 [재삗]이에요.

phrases.en: The economy is bad, so next year's outlook is bleak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞날이 밝지 않고 어둡다는 비유로 뉴스나 글에서 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say the future looks dim, used in news and writing.

explain_en: It is a dull ash gray, not black. It is often used for gloomy scenes like skies, clouds, seas and cities, while the everyday color name is '회색'. It is pronounced [재삗].

examples.en: If you leave clothes in the washer too long, they get wrinkly.
Grandma's hands are wrinkled, but they are warm.
I flattened the crumpled paper with an iron.
The apple is old, so its skin has shriveled.
I was in the water so long that my fingers are wrinkly.
I threw away the tangerine that had dried up and shriveled.

explain: 마르거나 오그라들어서 주름이 많이 진 모양에 써요. 옷이나 종이가 구겨진 건 '구깃구깃하다'나 '구겨지다'라고도 해요. 사람 피부에는 '주름이 많다'고 말하는 쪽이 부드러워요.

phrases.en: Even a wrinkly apple tastes fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 주름이 많은 물건을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a noun to describe something with many wrinkles.

phrases.en: I ironed it, so the shirt isn't wrinkled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 주름이 없고 펴진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something is smooth with no wrinkles.

phrases.en: The paper dried up all wrinkled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로, 어떻게 되었는지 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, used to describe how something ended up looking.

explain_en: It describes something with many wrinkles because it dried out or shrank. For crumpled clothes or paper, people also say '구깃구깃하다' or '구겨지다'. For a person's skin, saying '주름이 많다' sounds gentler.

examples.en: My son is a well-known rascal in the neighborhood.
The mischievous kids are playing in the dirt.

examples.ko: 그 개구쟁이가 또 창문에 공을 던졌어요.
examples.en: That rascal threw a ball at the window again.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 저는 장난이 심한 개구쟁이였어요.
examples.en: As a child I was a rascal who played a lot of pranks.
His mischievous smile is really cute.

examples.ko: 개구쟁이 동생 때문에 집이 조용할 날이 없어요.
examples.en: Because of my rascal of a brother, the house is never quiet.

explain: 장난이 심하지만 밉지 않은 아이를 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요. 나쁜 행동을 하는 '문제아'와 달리 애정이 담겨 있어요. 보통 어린 남자아이에게 많이 쓰지만 여자아이에게도 써요.

phrases.en: I often laugh because of my playful younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개구쟁이'와 비슷하게 장난이 많은 아이를 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 개구쟁이, affectionately calling a playful child.

phrases.en: His smiling face looks mischievous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 아이의 장난기 있는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a playful look on a child or an adult.

phrases.en: A mischievous boy is playing in the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 글에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing common in stories and writing.

explain_en: An affectionate word for a child who plays many pranks but is not disliked. Unlike 문제아, which suggests bad behavior, 개구쟁이 carries fondness. It is most often used for young boys but also for girls.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 고집쟁이라서 한번 싫다고 하면 끝이에요.
examples.en: My son is stubborn, so once he says no, that's it.
That child has been stubborn since he was little.

examples.ko: 고집쟁이 친구를 설득하느라 한 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to persuade my stubborn friend.
I often get called stubborn.

examples.ko: 고집쟁이처럼 굴지 말고 한번 들어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't be so stubborn, just give it a listen.
My grandmother is a bit of a cute stubborn person.

explain: 거짓말쟁이, 욕심쟁이처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙은 말은 그런 성격을 가진 사람을 가리켜요. '고집불통'보다 가벼워서 아이나 가까운 사람에게 장난스럽게도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A stubborn child isn't easy to calm down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이에게 쓰면 장난스럽고 가벼운 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a child, it sounds playful and light.

phrases.example: 그만 고집을 부리고 제 말을 들어 보세요.
phrases.en: Stop being stubborn and listen to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 생각만 계속 내세우는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the act of insisting on one's own way.

phrases.example: 우리 딸은 고집이 세서 한번 싫다고 하면 안 해요.
phrases.en: My daughter is stubborn, so once she says no, she won't do it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 바로 '고집쟁이'라고 부르지 않고 성격을 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the personality gently without calling the person a '고집쟁이'.

explain_en: Words ending in '-쟁이', like 거짓말쟁이 and 욕심쟁이, name a person with that trait. It is lighter than '고집불통', so it can be used playfully with children or close people.
